note: One record per golden. 'verdict' is accept|refuse; 'check' says how tools/check-games-goldens.py decides it: 'schema' (spec/games/schemas/*.json alone), 'semantic' (a small rule the checker runs in addition to the schema, named in 'rule'), or 'pinned' (this repo can only assert the golden PARSES/schema-validates; the real refusal needs a real folder tree, a real zip, or the signed catalogue's ownership table, and is lane L's or lane C's test to run -- named in 'enforced_by').

Its own list on purpose: launcher 0.5.0's K17 reads `builtin` and `hostile` above and nothing here, so these goldens cannot change a 0.5.0 answer. `client` is what a client that evaluates `mods` does (§7.9: an error inside the table drops only `mods`); `reader_ignoring_mods` is what a reader that reads nothing in it (launcher 0.5.0) answers for the whole descriptor; `verdict` is ingest's and lint's.

invalid.note: a text_id is dot-separated segments [a-z][a-z0-9_-]* (market.rights.animations); an empty segment is refused.

valid.name: lift-near-miss
valid.note: six lifts, each one member away from the security row the list still carries (versions by one byte, lifts_at by one second, entry_id absent, another repo_id, versions with a space inside, versions with a space before): none names the row, so the list is not contradicted and the row stays in force. versions is read byte for byte, with no trim

valid.name: rows-dropped
valid.note: no row and `lifts: []`: the member may be present and empty

valid.name: lift-no-row
valid.note: a lift and no row: the lifted row left `rows` in the issue that carries its lift

valid.name: lift-entry-id-as-a-client-reads-it
valid.note: a lift whose entry_id is ' Someone/PEAK-Astra ': a client trims and lowercases it, so it names the row of someone/peak-astra (scenario entry-id-as-a-client-reads-it)

valid.name: cascade-banner-and-yank
valid.note: the two rows ONE act writes for one subject, a cascade's banner (deprecate) and its yank, share their at: the one pair one-act-per-second allows

scenarios.name: sticky-security-revoke
scenarios.note: games-withdrawn-v1.md §2.2. The rows in force on a client after it verifies each list in turn (strictly rising serials). A yank and a delist retract when a later list omits them; the security revoke does not: six near-miss lifts release nothing, dropping the row releases nothing, and only the lift whose subject is the row's as written and whose lifts_at is the row's at releases it.

scenarios.name: lift-contradicted-row-wins
scenarios.note: a list that carries a row and a lift naming it is a publisher defect (lift-not-contradicted, the signer refuses to sign it); a client that meets one anyway lets the ROW win

scenarios.name: entry-id-as-a-client-reads-it
scenarios.note: §2.2, the first reading rule: entry_id is trimmed and lowercased before it is compared, in a row and in a lift alike, so ' Someone/PEAK-Astra ' names the row of someone/peak-astra and releases the security revoke

scenarios.name: unreadable-row-retracts-nothing
scenarios.note: a row whose entry_id is empty once trimmed cannot be keyed. A client reports it and, while the list carries it, retracts NOTHING: the yank and the delist the list omits stay in force with the security revoke. This is why the publisher never writes one (entry-id-readable)

scenarios.name: unreadable-lift-is-skipped
scenarios.note: a lift whose entry_id holds a control character is skipped and the rest of the list is read: the yank and the delist retract because the list omits them, and the security revoke stays because nothing named it

content.note: manifest.md §2.7 / dev/game-integrations-plan-merged.md §5.4: the content-coverage check (E_CONTENT_UNDECLARED/MISSING/DUPLICATE) and the HARD VRM licence gate (E_CONTENT_LICENCE_REFUSED). These need real bytes, not only a parsed manifest, so they are not schema/semantic goldens over a lone TOML file like the rest of this document -- 'releases' pairs a manifest with the real content-typed files its release zip would hold, and 'vrm_gate' is the gate alone, over a tiny synthetic GLB. check-games-goldens.py's own find_content_files/content_coverage/vrm_gate_refusal and the catalogue's lib/content.mjs are independent implementations of the same rule (manifest.md §4's exception note).

vrm_gate.name: allowed
vrm_gate.note: 0.x, isolates neither trigger: licenseName=CC_BY (a UniVRM token; O-2c), allowedUserName=Everyone, plus the usage flags

vrm_gate.name: allowed-vrm1
vrm_gate.note: 1.0, same shape as 'allowed' plus its own usage flags

vrm_gate.name: refused-vrm1-redistribution-string
vrm_gate.note: O-2b: the string "true" is not a bool -- prohibited

vrm_gate.name: refused-vrm0-absent-fields
vrm_gate.note: meta present but empty -- UniVRM's own absent-licenseName default is prohibited

vrm_gate.name: refused-vrm1-absent-fields
vrm_gate.note: meta present but empty -- the VRM 1.0 meta schema's own absent-allowRedistribution default is false

vrm_gate.name: unknown-no-meta
vrm_gate.note: a valid GLB with no VRM/VRMC_vrm extension at all -- G4: flagged, never refused

vrm_gate.name: unknown-vrm0-licence-other
vrm_gate.note: O-2b: Other means the terms are elsewhere -- unknown, never allowed (the content contract's vrm0-licence-other)

vrm_gate.name: unknown-vrm0-licence-unrecognised
vrm_gate.note: O-2b/O-2c: no UniVRM LicenseType, not CC0/CC_* -- what allowed.vrm carried until it was corrected

vrm_gate.name: unknown-vrm0-user-unrecognised
vrm_gate.note: O-2b: an unrecognised permission token is unknown, never allowed

vrm_gate.name: unknown-vrm1-avatar-unrecognised
vrm_gate.note: O-2b: an unrecognised permission token is unknown, never allowed

vrm_gate.name: metas-disagree
vrm_gate.note: O-2: VRM 0.x meta allows (licenseName=CC_BY, allowedUserName=Everyone); VRM 1.0 meta prohibits (allowRedistribution=false). A reader that stops at the first meta found would pass it.

vrm_gate.name: metas-agree
vrm_gate.note: both a VRM 0.x and a VRM 1.0 meta present, both allow and their overlapping usage flags (violent, sexual) agree -- reading both must still pass

vrm_gate.name: metas-unknown-vs-allowed
vrm_gate.note: O-2b: VRM 0.x reads unknown (licenseName=Other), VRM 1.0 reads allowed -- an unknown against an allowed is a conflict

vrm_gate.name: vrm-duplicate-key
vrm_gate.note: allowRedistribution false then true: one reader's false is another's true

vrm_gate.name: glb-duplicate-extensions
vrm_gate.note: two `extensions` members: refused before classification, never read as plain

vrm_gate.name: vrm-chunk-past-eof
vrm_gate.note: the JSON chunk is declared 8 bytes longer than the file (the content catalogue's vrm-chunk-past-eof)

vrm_gate.name: vrm-header-length-wrong
vrm_gate.note: the GLB header's total length is not the file's size

vrm_gate.name: glb-remote-uri
vrm_gate.note: a GLB carries everything it needs; an https image uri would make Astra fetch it (the content catalogue's glb-remote-uri)

vrm_gate.name: glb-data-uri
vrm_gate.note: a data: uri is not external; a plain GLB has no VRM meta
